subject: Audit record lifecycles — retention windows, export formats, and deletion proofing
messages:
From: Julia Hammond <julia.hammond@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-19T15:12:00Z
Subject: Questions on audit/access log retention and exports

Hi Michael / Marissa,

We're preparing for an upcoming audit and need to understand Redwood's capabilities around audit and access logs. Specifically:
- What are the default retention windows for API access logs and tenant audit trails in the EU region?
- Can we pull a full export (raw events) covering arbitrary date ranges, and what formats do those exports come in?
- Do you provide any proof-of-deletion / tamper-evidence when logs are purged?
- What's the expected lead time and SLA for a bulk export request (e.g., a 12 month slice)?

We're on a tight timeline — can you share a short description and any sample manifests or schemas?

Thanks,
Julia Hammond
Head of Security Operations
Acme Health

[External attachment: audit-questions-acme-20270519.docx]
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Hammond <julia.hammond@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-19T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention and exports

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, then I'll loop in the export/infra owners for the details and an estimated turnaround: 

- Default retention (EU tenant): 180 days for audit traces (management plane events) and 365 days for system access logs by default; both can be extended under enterprise contracts.
- Exports: Yes — we support bulk exports of raw events (newline-delimited JSON) and a columnar CSV summary for quick review. Exports include an index manifest with checksums.
- Deletion proofing: We provide an export manifest and an attestation file that captures the snapshot time, file checksums, and the deletion action id. For contract-level legalhold cases we can provide a signed attestation.
- SLA/lead time: Standard bulk export requests are completed within 7 business days for up to 3TB of compressed data; larger requests or legal-hold deliveries are coordinated with the Customer Success/Support team and may take longer.

I'll attach a retention matrix and a sample manifest; Marissa / Priyom will add technical notes about incremental snapshots and export formats.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: retention-matrix-ACME.pdf]
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention and exports

Michael / team — adding the export mechanics and format specifics Julia asked for.

- Formats:
  * Raw events: newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each event includes a stable event_id, timestamp (RFC3339), tenant_id, user_id (if available), action, resource, and metadata blob.
  * Summary CSV: pre-aggregated rows (timestamp, event_type, src_ip, user_agent, resource_id) for quick ingestion into SIEM.

- Integrity: Exports include a manifest.json with sha256 checksums for each file and a top-level manifest.sig (RSA-4096) when requested for attestation.

- Incremental snapshots: We support both full-range exports and incremental windows. For ongoing replication, we can deliver daily deltas (compressed) with sequence numbers so you can reconstruct a continuous stream.

- Deletion workflow: When a retention window elapses, files are moved to a short-term staging area (48–72 hours) and then securely deleted. For evidence we record a deletion_event with deletion_id and include that id in the attestation file you receive. For customers requiring stronger guarantees, we can deliver an HSM-signed attestation (requires enterprise contract).

- Performance notes: A 30-day NDJSON export for an active tenant (~100M events) is typically ~120GB compressed; we parallelize extraction by shard and stage as signed, chunked archives in an S3 bucket (pre-authorized URL) or push to your SFTP.

Let me know if we should schedule a short call to map exact ranges and transfer method.

—Karthik
Senior Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

[Attachment: audit-export-schema.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention and exports

Hi Julia — following up with proposed next steps to kick off the export and evidence package: 

1) Confirm scope: date range (start/end), tenant ids, list of event types you want (we can include management plane + access + token events).
2) Delivery preference: pre-signed S3 URLs to your bucket or SFTP push to your endpoint.
3) Attestation level: standard manifest (sha256 + internal signature) or HSM-signed attestation (contract).

If you can reply with the scope and preferred transfer method we'll open a ticket and target a 5–7 business day delivery for the size you described.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
